On January 30th, the flip Windows handheld console AYANEO FLIP KB & DS was officially released

notes: Dimensions and mass come from AYANEO's own spec-sheet IMAGE on the ayaneo.com product page (the page body itself is JS-driven and carries no text specs; the spec table is rendered as image .../product/2024/FLIP/DS/6_02.jpg, read visually). AYANEO prints one size only: '180*102*29.8mm (37.5mm at the grip)' — that is the folded/closed state, so it is recorded under dimensions_mm.closed and dimensions_mm.open is left null (AYANEO publishes no open-state dimension). The 37.5mm 'at the grip' figure is a local maximum over the grips, NOT a hinge thickness, so depth_at_hinge is left null. AXIS ORDERING: AYANEO lists 180 first; 180mm is the long edge (the horizontal edge when the device is held), recorded as `height` per the spec's 'long axis as the OEM lists it' rule — note this is the device's landscape width in normal use. displays[0].resolution_px is AYANEO's own '1080P' = 1920x1080; AYANEO does not print the pixel dimensions explicitly for this model. DISCREPANCY: the same AYANEO table prints '368 PPI' for the main screen, which is inconsistent with 7in/1920x1080 (=314.7 PPI); AYANEO's own FLIP 1S DS table prints 315 PPI for an identically specified 7in 1920x1080 panel, so the 368 figure appears to be an error on AYANEO's Flip DS sheet — recorded here only in the source quote, not used. active_area_mm derived from sourced diagonal + sourced resolution: width = 25.4*D*w/hypot(w,h), height = 25.4*D*h/hypot(w,h); assumes the stated diagonal is exact (OEMs round). Panel type: AYANEO says IPS for both screens, recorded as LCD per the schema enum. stick/trigger/bumper counts are NOT stated by AYANEO and are left null rather than guessed (AYANEO names 'Hall Sensing Joystick', 'Linear Hall Trigger' and 'shoulder buttons' without counts); abxy=4 and dpad=1 follow directly from the names AYANEO uses. Ports: two distinct USB-C ports (1x full-feature USB4 40Gbps, 1x USB 3.2 Gen2 data-only) are recorded as two usb_c entries; AYANEO also lists a 1x OCuLink SFF-8612 port, which has no kind in the schema enum and is recorded only here. RELEASED left null on purpose: AYANEO stated only shipping WINDOWS, not dates — 'The AMD Ryzen 7 7840U version ... expected to start shipping in the middle of March, while the AMD Ryzen 7 8840U version is planned to begin shipping in the end of April' (2024) — no day-precision date was ever published, so a released date would have been a guess. ANNOUNCED: 2024-01-30 is AYANEO's own 'officially released' launch article; a preceding CEO product-sharing session was held 2024-01-03 (ayaneo.com/article/804) and the product was teased earlier still, so 2024-01-30 is the full-spec/pricing reveal rather than first mention. hinge.free_stop=true from 'Full-angle Hovering'; note AYANEO's launch article additionally describes detents that auto-lock at 120°/150°/180°, so hovering coexists with three preset stops. The ayaneo.com FLIP DS product page currently shows status 'Coming Soon' and the model is no longer listed on AYANEO's own store (shop.ayaneo.com) — the spec image is still served and is the source used here. external_ids.igdb_platform null: this is a Windows PC, not an IGDB games platform.
